notes: One file for both rooms: identical shell, furniture, camera and slot positions; the girl room is the boy room shifted exactly +3.63 in Y. plan_m is given for the boy room (girl: add 3.63 to every Y). Slots with 'rooms' exist in one room only. category = Bible controlled vocabulary (textile, lighting, ceramics-tableware, storage-function, art-decor-toys); fixed-product furniture is storage-function. placement uses the product-card enum; placement_detail names the surface. z = layer order bottom to top; shadow at z-1 unless has_shadow_layer is false. Tie-break: product layers that share a z never overlap by design (if they do, the one nearer the camera goes on top; toy-cars and doll share z 46 but never share a room); shadow layers are multiply and order-independent; no product shares its z with a shadow layer. envelope_cm = max envelope per variant; 3 variants within +-15%. frames = master frames where the product is visible by design. Every toy and kid product passes the safety gate (Bible 1.6) before rating. hotspot and zoom_frame after the shell render.

density.rule: Bible 1.7.1 S11: lean frame, minimum 11 is a floor; as many as the designer judges do not detract (the right side is already the busy side: no additions). Counted (rule D1, 2026-10-10, with user decision D1B, 2026-10-11) = a slot whose product is >= 50% visible and covers >= 0.5% of the frame; a set counts once; fixed-product furniture counts under the same rule (D1B: here bed and desk, while they are for sale under D7); not counted: fillers, shell, fixed furniture that is not sold. A frame still short gets sold products from docs/proposals/density-after-d1.md (D1B).
